out.summary: TCS is India's largest IT services company, reporting Q2 FY27 (Sept 2026) revenue of ₹73,188 crore with 0.5% QoQ constant-currency growth and 24% operating margin. Growth is broadening across international markets and AI revenue crossed $3.1 billion annualized (over 10% of revenue), though margins face investment and MHP-related headwinds.
out.how_it_makes_money: Revenue comes from IT services across verticals — BFSI (largest, +2.5% QoQ), Manufacturing, Technology & Services, Consumer Business, Life Sciences, and ERU — plus regional markets including India; AI services now exceed 10% of overall revenue.

bull.point: AI revenue scaling fast and at higher margins than company average
bull.quote: the $3.1 billion AI revenues which we have are coming in at a much higher margin than our company average

bull.point: Broad-based international growth with strong BFSI
bull.quote: BFSI was our strongest large vertical and the largest contributor to growth, with 2.5% sequential and 3.9% year-on-year growth in constant currency

bull.point: Healthy order book excluding large pending deals
bull.quote: TCV for the quarter was US$9.6 billion. This excludes the Porsche and Best Buy deals

bear.point: Margin path to 25-26% uncertain amid rising subcontracting and investment costs
bear.quote: While it's an uphill task, we'll continue to endeavor to inch up on our margins

bear.point: MHP acquisition dilutes margins ~50bps in H2
bear.quote: The acquisition-related dilution, particularly in MHP, is likely to impact by about 50 basis points depending on the timing of closure

bear.point: AI deflation risk not yet over; Consumer and ERU declined
bear.quote: I don't want to conclude by saying that the deﬂation part is complete

watch.point: Whether India project deferral revenue returns and regional markets stabilize
watch.quote: In India, we had a project deferral, which caused this revenue decrease

watch.point: Whether margins can inch toward 25% exit FY27 despite headwinds
watch.quote: we'd look towards inching up from where we are, whilst not losing sight of prioritizing investments for growth
